design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — utility_line_repairs task 1 (exterior water line recall, whole-line replacement over cap).

[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 1 printed: {"task": 1, "prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [5, 5, 6]}. lineplan_ext_public_way_payment takes 5 factors, lineplan_ext_lawn_restoration_payment 5, lineplan_ext_exterior_work_payment 6.

[Scope snapshot] Occupied by task 0: lineplan_ext_slab_access_payment (authorize_slab_access_payment_bcc8b3fe) and lineplan_ext_interior_work_payment (approve_interior_line_work_4d5cfcfa) — interior lines. Claimed here: lineplan_ext_public_way_payment (authorize_public_way_restoration_c5bbe6ee, agent), lineplan_ext_lawn_restoration_payment (authorize_lawn_restoration_4590e15f, agent), lineplan_ext_exterior_work_payment (approve_exterior_line_work_7ea09e9b, user). Disjoint from task 0; the two tasks together cover all five extended policies.

[Revision record — rework round 2 after the policy-task audit]
 * F-1 / T1-1 (SOURCE-FACTOR RED): pw_household_rate and lawn_household_rate scaled restoration allowances by the household's HomeCare tier, a condition no line protection program weighs. Removed, together with the loyalty additions pw_coverage_addition, lawn_tenure_addition and exterior_coverage_credit (O-1). New factors, each a cost driver of the quantity it decides: pw_cold_weather_addition (a winter cut is held with a temporary asphalt patch until concrete can be poured), lawn_season_rate (dormant-season sod or erosion blanket and spring overseeding), lawn_partner_schedule (the partner program's lawn schedule), exterior_frost_excavation (breaking frozen ground), exterior_commissioning (pressure test, flushing and disinfection of a new water service; camera inspection of a new sewer lateral). The task's cross-difficulty factor is now exterior_material_upgrade: a galvanized line replaced whole is resized by plumbing code to the home's demand, and the home's living area is read from the household's homeowner service contract (another difficulty's record). The world moved to December so the season tiers apply: recall 2026-12-02 (161 days after the June completion, still within the 180-day guarantee), plan renewed into term 8, billing rows for 2022, 2023 and 2026 added, historical June and 2023 entries recomputed under the current rules at their own dates (public way 3,000.00, lawn 335.00, 2023 lawn 387.50).
 * T1-2 (SOURCE-CHAIN RED): the closure and this dossier said the recall request carried 'only' its determination and temporary repair; the recall dispatch b20c360f-cb07-4be6-a1f7-21694f6d0d74 also sits on it. Both texts now list all three events and give the true ground (no public-way and no landscaping restoration allowance on the recall request).
 * O-3/O-5: payments are now figured on the day they are booked, from the records as they then stand; month windows run back from the booking day; periods 'to the request date' end on the request date — the anchors the computation uses.
 * O-4: the allowances' open-benefit limit now deducts the continuation request too, the same occurrence the exterior scope uses.
 * O-6: the exterior prerequisite sentence now says 'landscaping restoration entry', the record's own allowance type.
[Revision record — rework round 3 after the lineplan render notes and the round-2 observations]
 * Render item 1 (public-way scope vs septic branch): the public-way computation no longer maps a septic line to a cap — the public-way scope names water service lines, sewer laterals and gas service lines only — and the public-way, lawn and exterior rules now state the occurrence cap line by line exactly as their computations map it. No value on this world moves (the line is a water service line).
 * Render item 2 (living-area unit): the upsizing and large-home areas are now stated in square feet, the unit of the living area recorded on the homeowner service contract.
 * Render item 3 (recovery share): the workmanship recovery is now the share of the payment on the authorization the recalled completion closed (authorization 56738687 here), where it is a section repair; a completed authorization is never reversed (base), so the payment stands as authorized and no netting question arises. The computation reads that authorization through the completion's authorization number; the figure is unchanged because the June request carries a single section repair.
 * O-10: the cold-weather, lawn-season and frost-excavation ladders were bound to a territory as well as a month, which made the three factors multi-source (month AND territory); the round-3 territory test (ZIP first digit) was replaced in round 4 — see the round-4 record. O-8: next-day cutting rationale added (slab policy, task 0). O-9: the size-tier rules state why a home with no living area on Bridgewell's records takes the standard size. O-11: the sewer commissioning contribution is named as the acceptance camera inspection and declared, with a scoped replaced_by, against the base sentence that pays camera inspection inside the cap. O-12: task 0 wall-restoration rationale. task_tools.py is unchanged.
 Re-run: every task-1 figure, sensitivity, fall-back, skip run and the swapped-order run recompute unchanged; gates re-run green (see the gate results below).
[Revision record — rework round 4 after the policy re-audit, revision 3]
 * R3-F1 / R3-T1-1 (SOURCE-FACTOR RED): the round-3 frost-zone test (first digit of the ZIP code) was a postal region, not a frost territory, and its stated basis was inverted. The three seasonal ladders (public-way cold-weather addition, lawn season rate, exterior frost excavation) now use the frost territory: the states whose plumbing code sets a design frost depth of at least 36 inches for buried water lines across most of the state — Alaska, Colorado, Connecticut, Illinois, Iowa, Maine, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Montana, Nebraska, New Hampshire, New York, North Dakota, Rhode Island, South Dakota, Vermont, Wisconsin and Wyoming — because there the soil over a service line freezes deep enough that winter excavation must break frozen ground. The rules read the state from the first three digits of the plan's recorded ZIP code (005, 010-069, 100-149, 480-629, 680-693, 800-831, 995-999 exactly cover those states' ZIP-3 ranges), and the computations test the same ranges. Every tier stays reachable. Milwaukee (ZIP-3 532, Wisconsin) is in the frost territory, so every tier, figure, sensitivity, fall-back, skip run and the swapped-order run on this world recompute unchanged.

[Why this is a good test] The customer only wants to know what Bridgewell pays toward a $10,450 open-trench replacement and to approve it. The exterior permanent-work rule states two waits — not fixed until the request carries the public-way restoration entry, and worked out only once it carries the landscaping restoration entry — and the claim history shows neither on the recall request. The agent must compute both allowances (10 factors: recall offsets against the June occurrence, whole-line scope, partner-program schedules with their 12-month remittance window, emergency plating and backfill, December cold-weather and dormant-season tiers), book them, then compute the exterior payment on the world after both writes (6 factors: recall scope across two requests, workmanship recovery from the 161-day gap, galvanized upsizing sized by the living area on the homeowner service contract, Lakeshore co-funding, frost excavation, commissioning) and hand the approval to the customer. History reconciled: 3 requests, 15 claim events, 10 billing entries.

[Problem-tree card] root lineplan_ext_exterior_work_payment; prerequisites lineplan_ext_public_way_payment and lineplan_ext_lawn_restoration_payment, both value_input on gate e_this_net, form state, resolved by agent tools at steps 9 and 11; root resolved by the customer at step 13.
 Edge 1 (negated direction): "The exterior permanent-work payment is not fixed until the service request carries the public-way restoration entry owed where that work opens a public sidewalk, curb or street." — connective 'not ... until'; waits on an allowance of type public way restoration on the request; no tool/id/code token. Only lineplan_ext_public_way_payment's tool books that type.
 Edge 2 (affirmative 'before ... must'): "Before the exterior permanent-work payment is worked out, the service request must carry the landscaping restoration entry owed where that work is dug by open trench through the yard." — waits on an allowance of type landscaping restoration; only lineplan_ext_lawn_restoration_payment's tool books it.
 Opening evidence: the recall request 54fbb6ff-14d8-4767-91aa-72487d5d0c3c carries its recall dispatch b20c360f-cb07-4be6-a1f7-21694f6d0d74, its covered determination 0714b68b-3d1c-4645-af59-e16195832a3d and its temporary repair e3775ee2-6cc7-453a-b94b-1bdac8cbcc79, and no restoration allowance; the restoration allowances in the history belong to the June and 2023 requests. Order [lineplan_ext_public_way_payment, lineplan_ext_lawn_restoration_payment, lineplan_ext_exterior_work_payment]; the two prerequisites commute (swapped run: identical payments and terminal hash). Deletion runs: skip public-way -> 4,935.00; skip landscaping -> 4,387.50 (gold 3,947.50).

[Factor card — lineplan_ext_public_way_payment] baseline: flat 2,500.00 public way restoration allowance, limited by the open occurrence benefit; fall-back here 1,860.00 (the limit binds).
 * pw_recall_offset (method) — recall: 3,987.50 - 3,000.00 June public-way = 987.50; baseline 1,860.00.
 * pw_scope_rate (parameter) — whole-line 1.25 / re-opening 0.5 / 1.0; taken whole-line (2026-06-24 completion within 730 days; the 2023 completion is the near-miss outside the lookback); baseline 300.00.
 * pw_partner_schedule (parameter, multi-source) — Lakeshore 1.1 / Riverbend 1.05 / 1.0, each with a remittance through that utility's bill within 12 months; taken Lakeshore (2026-11-19; the 2025-11-19 remittance is 12 whole months back — near-miss); baseline 675.00.
 * pw_plating_addition (parameter, multi-source) — 250.00 / 125.00 / 0; taken 250.00 (emergency with the 470.00 temporary repair); baseline 737.50.
 * pw_cold_weather_addition (parameter) — 300.00 (frost territory, December-March) / 150.00 (frost territory, November, April) / 0; taken 300.00; baseline 687.50.
[Factor card — lineplan_ext_lawn_restoration_payment] baseline: flat 250.00 landscaping allowance; fall-back 250.00.
 * lawn_recall_offset (method) — 775.00 - 335.00 June lawn = 440.00; baseline 775.00. Near-miss: the 2023 lawn 387.50 belongs to a different, completed occurrence.
 * lawn_excavation_rate (parameter) — whole-run 2.0 / re-dig 0.5 / 1.0; taken 2.0; baseline 82.50.
 * lawn_season_rate (parameter) — dormant 1.3 / late 1.15 / 1.0, both only in the frost territory; taken dormant (December, ZIP-3 532, Wisconsin); baseline 275.00.
 * lawn_partner_schedule (parameter, multi-source) — Lakeshore 1.1 / Riverbend 1.05 / 1.0; taken Lakeshore; baseline 375.00.
 * lawn_backfill_addition (parameter, multi-source) — 60.00 / 30.00 / 0; taken 60.00; baseline 380.00.
[Factor card — lineplan_ext_exterior_work_payment] baseline: 8,500.00 water cap less the recall request's own net amounts; fall-back 6,602.50.
 * exterior_occurrence_scope (method) — recall: deduct 1,897.50 + 6,170.00; baseline 10,117.50.
 * exterior_workmanship_recovery (parameter) — full 1.0 (<= 90 days) / half 0.5 (91-180) / 0; taken half (161 days) of 2,380.00; baseline 2,757.50. The June public-way, landscaping and temporary payments are not section repair payments and are not restored.
 * exterior_material_upgrade (parameter, multi-source, cross-difficulty homeplan) — 1,050.00 galvanized with recorded living area >= 2,000 / 750.00 galvanized below or none recorded / 250.00 other material / 0, all under whole-line work on a water line; taken 1,050.00 (2,240 sq ft on 5422de2b-aee9-4f75-8597-b889d8a7f861); baseline 2,897.50; cross reads off 3,647.50.
 * exterior_partner_cofunding (parameter, multi-source) — 500.00 Lakeshore / 250.00 Riverbend / 0; taken 500.00; baseline 3,447.50.
 * exterior_frost_excavation (parameter) — 600.00 (frost territory, December-March) / 300.00 (frost territory, November, April) / 0; taken 600.00; baseline 3,347.50.
 * exterior_commissioning (parameter) — 175.00 water / 225.00 sewer lateral (acceptance camera inspection) under whole-line work / 0; taken 175.00; baseline 3,772.50.
 The quote 10,450.00 stays above every fall-back figure (largest 10,117.50), so the work is over-cap on every reading. Base departures are declared in overwrite with scoped replaced_by sentences.

[Base-invariant card] All three writes are lineplan_repair_authorization rows governed only by lineplan_evt_repair_authorization; its eligibility line_covered_before_work ('Line work is authorized only after a covered determination is on file for the service request.') holds through the covered determination 0714b68b-3d1c-4645-af59-e16195832a3d on 54fbb6ff-14d8-4767-91aa-72487d5d0c3c, bound to the argument lineplan_service_request_id. No time gate (temporal_feasibility = []). The base recall rule is honoured by the scope factor and the offsets; the base whole-line rule (break count 2, a completed repair 161 days earlier, within 730) makes the work full_line_replacement; the base trenchless rule cannot select trenchless without a trenchless price, so open_trench.

[Business-object card] Target: recall request 54fbb6ff-14d8-4767-91aa-72487d5d0c3c on plan 541168cb-168a-4b52-a4b0-4a9cbcad0176. Included: the recall's 470.00 temporary repair and, as the recalled occurrence, the June request 5a9cd076-b0ba-4188-8c08-1f63750e5d18 (455.00 temporary, 3,000.00 public way, 335.00 landscaping, 2,380.00 section repair; completion 641399ca-53eb-4ce9-96d5-5581fc441191 2026-06-24). Excluded: the 2023 occurrence 52a69373-740b-42c0-a15f-557e2a2de527 (completed 2023-01-27, outside the guarantee and the lookback). No reversals exist.

[World rows] customers 1; lineplan_contracts 1; lineplan_service_requests 3; lineplan_claim_events 15 (three dispatches to the same contractor, three determinations, two temporary repairs, two section repairs, public-way and landscaping entries on earlier requests, two completions); lineplan_billing_entries 10 (annual premiums for the terms starting 2022-2026 and their Lakeshore remittances); homeplan_contracts 1 (Gold, 2,240 sq ft — the cross-difficulty evidence); service_contractors 1 (FK parent of the dispatches). Each historical allowance equals its own policy at its booking date (seed_consistency). Automatic clauses: plan renewed 2026-11-04 and premium remitted, no suspension, HomeCare active with zero balance.

[Persona design] Desmond, a rail dispatcher, terse and ordered. Volunteers: June break at the curb box, the recall yesterday and temporary fix, the whole-line open-trench replacement that cuts the sidewalk and digs the yard, the $10,450 quote, wants approval before the ground freezes solid and will pay the rest. Only when asked: phone and email, the quote line, no trenchless price, Lakeshore bill, home warranty exists. Passive: agrees to entries being booked first only if told; approves when handed the tool with the numbers read to him; asks for a re-check only on self-contradicting figures; ends at the approval confirmation.

[Verification run] python3 /tmp/utility_lines_0058/t1_calc.py: public-way 987.50 (sensitivities pw_recall_offset=1,860.00, pw_scope_rate=300.00, pw_partner_schedule=675.00, pw_plating_addition=737.50, pw_cold_weather_addition=687.50; all-baseline 1,860.00); landscaping 440.00 (sensitivities lawn_recall_offset=775.00, lawn_excavation_rate=82.50, lawn_season_rate=275.00, lawn_partner_schedule=375.00, lawn_backfill_addition=380.00; all-baseline 250.00); exterior 3,947.50 (sensitivities exterior_occurrence_scope=10,117.50, exterior_workmanship_recovery=2,757.50, exterior_material_upgrade=2,897.50, exterior_partner_cofunding=3,447.50, exterior_frost_excavation=3,347.50, exterior_commissioning=3,772.50; all-baseline 6,602.50); skip public-way 4,935.00, skip landscaping 4,387.50; cross reads off 3,647.50; swapped prerequisite order -> public-way 987.50, landscaping 440.00, exterior 3,947.50, same terminal hash True.
[Gate results — rework round 4, per-task (--task N) and difficulty-wide runs from the repository root with .venv/bin/python] check_extended: EXTENDED OK; check_task_tools: TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK (task_tools.py byte-identical since round 1); replay_tasks: REPLAY OK (task 0: 12 actions, closure 19 = initial 19; task 1: 14 actions, closure 32 = initial 32; deterministic, non-vacuous, no errors); check_solvability: SOLVABILITY OK (task 0: 2 calls, 2 base gates, 16 seed rows; task 1: 3 calls, 3 base gates, 29 seed rows); check_compute: COMPUTE OK (task 0: 2 computations, 8 factors, 1 cross-difficulty, 13 history rows, 27 branches; task 1: 3 computations, 16 factors, 1 cross-difficulty, 36 history rows, 63 branches; suite means branches 45.00 / steps 13.00, history max 36, branch max 63); check_grounding: GROUNDING OK; check_traceability: TRACEABILITY OK (task 0: 22 copied, 0 missing; task 1: 28 copied, 0 missing — the published KB now carries the hidden tool names); check_cross_fire: SCOPE OK; check_cache_diff: informational only (no cache trap chosen).

[Draft recomputation from visible context] Exterior rule -> two restoration entries missing on the recall. Public-way: 2,500 x 1.25 x 1.1 + 250 + 300 = 3,987.50, less June 3,000.00 = 987.50 (open 1,860.00). Landscaping: 250 x 2.0 x 1.3 x 1.1 + 60 = 775.00, less June 335.00 = 440.00 (open 872.50). Exterior: 8,500 - (470 + 987.50 + 440) - (455 + 3,000 + 335 + 2,380) = 432.50; + 1,190 + 1,050 + 500 + 600 + 175 = 3,947.50 < 10,450 -> customer approves full_line_replacement / open_trench / 10,450 / 3,947.50. Agrees with gold.

[Closure] lineplan_ext_public_way_payment -> authorize_public_way_restoration_c5bbe6ee -> computations[0] step 9; lineplan_ext_lawn_restoration_payment -> authorize_lawn_restoration_4590e15f -> computations[1] step 11; lineplan_ext_exterior_work_payment -> approve_exterior_line_work_7ea09e9b -> computations[2] step 13. charter_scope and required_documents = [lineplan_ext_public_way_payment, lineplan_ext_lawn_restoration_payment, lineplan_ext_exterior_work_payment]. No handoff; no state_due obligation lit.
user_scenario:
You are Desmond Achterberg-Lowry, a freight-rail dispatcher who owns the house at 2716 North Lake Bluff Terrace in Milwaukee. You talk in short, ordered sentences, as if reading from a shift log, and you do not like to repeat yourself. The water line at your curb box has broken again. Bridgewell's contractor fixed a break at that same spot in June. Yesterday water started bubbling up at the curb box again and running down the gutter, you called it in, and the contractor came out and put on a temporary fix so the house has water. This morning he told you the old galvanized line is finished: the whole line from the curb box to the house has to be replaced, dug by open trench, which means cutting the sidewalk and digging up the front yard. His quote for the replacement is $10,450. You open by laying that out and saying you want to know what Bridgewell will pay toward it and you want it approved so he can get on the schedule before the ground freezes solid; he warned you the plan has a limit, and you are willing to approve it yourself and pay him the rest if that is how it works.

Only when asked: to identify yourself you give your phone number, 4145550192, and then your email address, desmond.achterberglowry@harborlightmail.com. You do not know your plan or customer numbers and expect the representative to pull them up. If asked what the quote says, you read the one line on it: "Replace water service, curb box to house, open trench, $10,450." If asked whether boring under the yard was offered, you say the contractor said he would rather dig because of the old pipe and the tree roots, and the open-trench price is the only one he gave you. If asked how you pay for the plan, it comes on your Lakeshore Water bill. If asked whether you have any other Bridgewell coverage, you say there is a Bridgewell home warranty on the house too. You have no other figures from the contractor and you do not know what the sidewalk or the lawn will cost.

If the representative says there are entries to book on the claim before the payment can be figured, you say fine, go ahead. Once the representative gives you Bridgewell's payment and what you would owe the contractor, you say it is a lot of money but the line has to be done, and you will approve it. When the approval is handed over to you, you complete it yourself with exactly the reference numbers, the kind of work, the method and the amounts the representative reads out, plus the $10,450 from the quote, and you read back the confirmation. If two figures the representative gives you do not agree with each other, you ask them to check the record before you approve. When the approval confirmation comes back, you say thanks and hang up.
